title: Why a loop can become a performance problem
subtitle: Spot quadratic work before production traffic does
learning_objective: Recognize common time-complexity patterns and predict how work scales.

source_refs.title: Big-O Cheat Sheet
source_refs.supports: reference for common algorithm complexity; verify examples independently

scenes.title: 10× THE DATA
scenes.body: A feature works with 100 records and crawls with 10,000. The hidden cost may be nested work.

scenes.title: Count growth, not milliseconds
scenes.body: Big O describes how work grows with input size. A single pass is typically O(n); comparing every item with every other item can be O(n²).

scenes.title: A hidden nested loop
Practical move
scenes.body: Profile first, then inspect repeated scans, nested loops, and database calls inside loops. Real runtime also depends on constants and data shape.

scenes.question: If n increases from 1,000 to 10,000, how does n² work scale approximately?
scenes.explanation: Quadratic work grows with the square of input size. A 10× increase in n means roughly 100× as many pairwise operations.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Estimate how work grows with data size, then measure the real bottleneck.
